import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«342»

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 7

Does Ulam's sequence have positive density?
Can one explain the curious Fourier properties of Ulam's sequence?

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 7](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.1)
- [erdosproblems.com/342](https://www.erdosproblems.com/342)
-/

open Nat Set Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace Green7

/--
Does Ulam's sequence have positive density?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 42]
theorem green_7.variants.positive_density :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, Erdos342.IsUlamSequence a →
        Set.upperDensity (Set.range a) > 0 := by
  sorry

end Green7

findings.description: The RHS requires only positive upper density: limsup_N |range(a) ∩ [0,N)|/N > 0. It does not require a positive limiting natural density, or even positive lower density. I proved in Lean that this condition is exactly ¬(Set.range a).HasDensity 0. These notions differ in general: the union of the integer intervals [(2k)!, (2k+1)!) has upper density 1 and lower density 0. The cited sources do not establish an equivalence for the Ulam sequence. Green leaves “density” unqualified, and the companion zero-density question makes the upper-density interpretation defensible, so this is a modelling ambiguity rather than a definite misformalization.
findings.source_evidence: Green, 100 Open Problems, Problem 7, p. 5, asks “Does this sequence have positive density?” and attributes the question to Ulam: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf. Steinerberger, A Hidden Signal in the Ulam Sequence, §1, describes Ulam’s original question as asking “whether it is possible to determine the asymptotic density of the sequence”: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.00267 (v6 source). Neither passage explicitly specifies upper density.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify the intended density notion. If the intended question requires a positive asymptotic density, replace the conclusion with `(Set.range a).HasPosDensity`, equivalently `∃ d > 0, (Set.range a).HasDensity d`. If this is intentionally the weaker nonzero-density variant, retain the current formula but explicitly identify it as a positive-upper-density question; a separate natural-density variant could state the stronger reading.

reformulations.difference: The source speaks about a single, specified Ulam sequence; Lean quantifies over every function satisfying IsUlamSequence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The predicate fixes the seeds 1 and 2 and uniquely determines each subsequent term by the least eligible sum. Strong induction therefore proves that any two satisfying functions are equal. Existence is ensured by the greedy construction: the sum of the two largest previous terms is uniquely represented and exceeds the last term, so an eligible minimum always exists. Thus, for the source’s Ulam sequence u, `∀ a, IsUlamSequence a → P a` is equivalent to `P u`. The scratch file proves uniqueness, the equivalence for any specified u satisfying the predicate, and the next-term existence lemma.
